title: Mark Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Mark chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Mark Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Mark Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Mark 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Pharisees and scribes come from Jerusalem
The disciples eat with unwashen hands
Moses commands to honor father and mother
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisees and scribes come from Jerusalem
questions.explanation: This is stated in Mark 7:1, where it describes the gathering of the Pharisees and scribes.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees find fault with regarding Jesus' disciples?
options: They were eating bread with unwashen hands
They were not honoring their parents
questions.correctAnswer: They were eating bread with unwashen hands
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Mark 7:2, where it states they found fault with the disciples for eating with defiled hands.

questions.question: According to the Pharisees, what must Jews do before eating?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:3 states that all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not.

questions.question: What tradition did the Pharisees hold regarding eating after coming from the market?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:4 indicates that when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees ask Jesus about his disciples?
options: Why do they heal on the Sabbath?
Why do they eat with unwashen hands?
Why do they speak in parables?
questions.correctAnswer: Why do they eat with unwashen hands?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:5 shows that the Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus why his disciples did not walk according to the tradition of the elders.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the worship of the people?
questions.explanation: According to Mark 7:7, Jesus states that in vain do they worship him, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

questions.question: What commandment of God did Jesus reference regarding honoring parents?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:10 states that Moses said to honor thy father and mother.

questions.question: What does Corban refer to according to the Pharisees' tradition?
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:11, Jesus explains that if a man says to his father or mother that something is Corban, it means it is a gift.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees allow regarding a man’s duty to his parents?
options: He can declare his wealth as Corban
questions.correctAnswer: He can declare his wealth as Corban
questions.explanation: Mark 7:11 indicates that the Pharisees taught that if a man declares something as Corban, he shall be free from helping his parents.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees prevent a man from doing if he declared something as Corban?
options: Doing anything for his father or mother
questions.correctAnswer: Doing anything for his father or mother
questions.explanation: Mark 7:12 states that they suffer him no more to do anything for his father or mother if he declares it Corban.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about the effect of tradition on the word of God?
options: It makes it of none effect
questions.correctAnswer: It makes it of none effect
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:13, Jesus says that making the word of God of none effect through their tradition is what they do.

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees came from Jerusalem to question Jesus.
questions.explanation: This fact is confirmed in Mark 7:1, where it states that the Pharisees and certain scribes came from Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that the people honored Him with their hearts.
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:6, Jesus mentions that the people honor Him with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him.

questions.question: True or False: Moses commanded the people to disregard their parents.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:10 states the opposite; Moses commanded to honor father and mother, not to disregard them.

questions.question: True or False: The tradition of the elders was not important to the Pharisees.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:3 and 7:5 show that the tradition of the elders was very important to the Pharisees.

medium.title: Mark Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Mark Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about what can defile a man?
options: Things that come from within him
Things that enter him from outside
questions.correctAnswer: Things that come from within him
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that 'That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man' (Mark 7:20).

questions.question: What does Mark 7:15 promise will happen if someone understands Jesus' teaching?
questions.explanation: Jesus calls people to hear and understand, implying that understanding leads to truth (Mark 7:14).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the things that enter a man?
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that 'whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him' (Mark 7:18).

questions.question: What does Mark 7:19 indicate about what happens to food that enters the body?
options: It goes out into the draught
questions.correctAnswer: It goes out into the draught
questions.explanation: Jesus states that food 'entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught' (Mark 7:19).

questions.question: According to Mark 7:21, from where do evil thoughts proceed?
questions.explanation: Jesus identifies that 'from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts' (Mark 7:21).

questions.question: What is associated with the concept of defilement in Mark 7:23?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that 'All these evil things come from within, and defile the man' (Mark 7:23).

questions.question: What did Jesus do after teaching the crowd?
questions.explanation: After addressing the crowd, 'he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house' (Mark 7:24).

questions.question: What did the Syrophenician woman do when she approached Jesus?
questions.explanation: The woman 'came and fell at his feet' as an act of humility and desperation (Mark 7:25).

questions.question: What was the nationality of the woman who approached Jesus?
questions.explanation: The woman was identified as 'a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation' (Mark 7:26).

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the disciples' lack of understanding?
options: He asked if they were without understanding
questions.correctAnswer: He asked if they were without understanding
questions.explanation: Jesus questioned, 'Are ye so without understanding also?' indicating his disappointment (Mark 7:18).

questions.question: What is the significance of having ears to hear according to Mark 7:16?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized, 'If any man have ears to hear, let him hear', highlighting the importance of understanding his teachings (Mark 7:16).

questions.question: What kind of spirit did the woman's daughter have?
questions.explanation: The text states that the woman’s daughter had 'an unclean spirit' (Mark 7:25).

questions.question: The statement 'This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me' reflects what concept?
questions.explanation: This statement illustrates the disconnect between outward worship and inner devotion, as quoted from Isaiah (Mark 7:6).

questions.question: According to Mark 7:8, the Pharisees held what above the commandment of God?
questions.explanation: They rejected the commandment of God to keep their own tradition, which is contrary to holding it above (Mark 7:9).

questions.question: Jesus’ teaching suggests that external actions are more important than the condition of one’s heart.
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that it is what comes from within that defiles a man, indicating the importance of the heart over external actions (Mark 7:20-23).

hard.title: Mark Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Mark Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean by saying, 'Let the children first be filled'?
questions.explanation: This reflects Jesus' initial mission to the Israelites before reaching out to the Gentiles, as stated in Mark 7:27.

questions.question: What was the response of the woman to Jesus' statement about the dogs?
questions.explanation: Her response in Mark 7:28 shows her humility and faith, acknowledging even the crumbs are valuable.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the woman after her response?
options: Your faith has healed your daughter
The devil is gone out of your daughter
questions.correctAnswer: The devil is gone out of your daughter
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:29, Jesus commends her faith and assures her that her daughter is healed.

questions.question: What was found when the woman returned home?
options: Her daughter was asleep and healed
questions.correctAnswer: Her daughter was asleep and healed
questions.explanation: Mark 7:30 describes how she found her daughter laid upon the bed, indicating healing.

questions.question: What condition did the man brought to Jesus have?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:32 specifically states that he was deaf and had an impediment in his speech.

questions.question: What method did Jesus use to heal the deaf man?
options: He used saliva and touched his tongue
questions.correctAnswer: He used saliva and touched his tongue
questions.explanation: Mark 7:33 shows that Jesus used his fingers and saliva as part of the healing process.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'Ephphatha' mean in Mark 7:34?
questions.explanation: The term 'Ephphatha' in Mark 7:34 means 'be opened', indicating the opening of the man's ears.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Mark 7:37 when they say, 'He hath done all things well'?
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the greatness of Jesus' works and is an example of repetition to enhance meaning.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of healing in Mark 7:29?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of healing through the Messiah, paralleling Jesus' healing actions in Mark 7:29.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of faith leading to healing, similar to Mark 7:30?
questions.explanation: Matthew 9:22 demonstrates the connection of faith leading to healing, echoing the woman's faith in Mark 7:30.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jesus' statement about the dogs in Mark 7:27?
options: Jesus was teaching in a synagogue
questions.explanation: Mark 7:26 describes how the woman approached Jesus, setting the context for His response in 7:27.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'from without' in Mark 7:15?
questions.explanation: Mark 7:15 uses 'from without' to highlight that external actions don't defile; rather, the heart does.

questions.question: The healing of the deaf man in Mark 7:35 demonstrates Jesus' power over which spiritual force?
questions.explanation: The healing in Mark 7:35 shows Jesus' authority over physical ailments, reflecting His divine power.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus encouraged the people to keep quiet about the miracles He performed.
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:36, Jesus charged them to tell no man about the miracle, indicating His desire for discretion.

questions.question: True or False: The deaf man could speak perfectly after Jesus healed him.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:35 states he spake plain, indicating improvement, but not necessarily perfection in speech.

theological.title: Mark Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Mark Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 7:6 teach about human sin?
options: Hypocrisy is a sin that separates the heart from God.
Human sin is primarily external and ritualistic.
Sin is only a matter of ignorance, not willful rebellion.
God ignores hypocrisy when people honor Him with their lips.
questions.correctAnswer: Hypocrisy is a sin that separates the heart from God.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:6 quotes Isaiah, showing that people may honor God with words while their hearts are far from Him, highlighting the sin of hypocrisy.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 7:10 teach about the authority of God's commandments?
options: God's commandments hold ultimate authority over human traditions.
Human traditions can override God's commandments.
God's commandments are flexible according to culture.
Traditions have equal authority as divine law.
questions.correctAnswer: God's commandments hold ultimate authority over human traditions.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:10 reiterates the commandment from Moses about honoring parents, demonstrating the enduring authority of God's law over traditions.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 7:23 teach about the nature of defilement?
options: True defilement arises from moral corruption within the human heart.
Defilement is caused only by eating unclean foods.
External ritual impurity determines spiritual status.
Defilement is a social construct unrelated to sin.
questions.correctAnswer: True defilement arises from moral corruption within the human heart.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:23 lists evil thoughts and actions that come from within, showing that defilement is a matter of internal sin, not external ritual.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Mark 7:34 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Mark 7:34, Jesus commands the deaf man to be opened, demonstrating His power to heal and perform miracles, reflecting divine omnipotence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Mark 7:29 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jesus grants the Syrophenician woman's request in Mark 7:29, showing God's mercy towards Gentiles.

questions.question: How does Mark 7:15 connect to the theme of justification by faith elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It teaches that external rituals do not defile, supporting justification by faith rather than works.
It emphasizes strict adherence to ritual purity for salvation.
It rejects faith as necessary for justification.
It teaches that dietary laws are essential for righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that external rituals do not defile, supporting justification by faith rather than works.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:15's teaching that nothing external can defile aligns with Pauline doctrine that justification is by faith, not works of the law.

questions.question: How does the healing of the deaf man in Mark 7:32-35 prepare for the universal mission of the church?
options: It shows Jesus' power to restore communication, symbolizing the church's role to proclaim the gospel to all nations.
It restricts Jesus' ministry to only Jewish people.
It focuses solely on physical healing without spiritual implications.
It emphasizes ritual cleansing as a prerequisite for healing.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus' power to restore communication, symbolizing the church's role to proclaim the gospel to all nations.
questions.explanation: The healing in Mark 7:32-35 symbolizes restoration of hearing and speech, prefiguring the church’s mission to spread the gospel worldwide.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Mark 7:15 and Mark 7:23 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification is an internal transformation of heart and not based on external observances.
Sanctification depends solely on external rituals and dietary laws.
Sanctification is unnecessary for the believer.
Sanctification is achieved by strict tradition keeping.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is an internal transformation of heart and not based on external observances.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:15 shows external things do not defile, and 7:23 identifies internal evil as the true defilement, teaching sanctification as internal heart change.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 7:6 and Mark 7:9 teach about the relationship between tradition and God's word?
options: Human traditions can invalidate the word of God when placed above it.
Traditions always enhance the word of God.
God's word is subordinate to human traditions.
Traditions have no impact on the word of God.
questions.correctAnswer: Human traditions can invalidate the word of God when placed above it.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:6 and 7:9 show Jesus condemns traditions that reject God's commandments, demonstrating that traditions can nullify God’s word.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 7:21 and Mark 7:22 teach about the source of moral evil?
options: Moral evil originates from within the human heart, manifesting in various sinful actions and attitudes.
Moral evil is caused primarily by external influences.
Moral evil is unrelated to human nature.
Moral evil is only external ceremonial impurity.
questions.correctAnswer: Moral evil originates from within the human heart, manifesting in various sinful actions and attitudes.
questions.explanation: Verses Mark 7:21 and 7:22 describe evil thoughts and sins proceeding from within the heart, teaching the internal nature of moral evil.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus' rebuke of traditions in Mark 7:1-13 undermines the validity of all religious tradition. What does Mark 7:1-13 actually teach?
options: It teaches that traditions which contradict God's commandments are invalid.
It teaches all traditions are equally authoritative with Scripture.
It rejects the use of any tradition in religious life.
It promotes traditions above God's law.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that traditions which contradict God's commandments are invalid.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:1-13 criticizes traditions that nullify God's word, affirming that divine commandments have precedence over human traditions.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 7:18 teach about spiritual understanding?
options: True understanding recognizes that external things cannot defile the heart.
Spiritual understanding is unnecessary for salvation.
External ritual purity is essential for spiritual understanding.
Only the Pharisees possessed true understanding.
questions.correctAnswer: True understanding recognizes that external things cannot defile the heart.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:18 shows Jesus rebuking his disciples for lack of understanding that defilement is not from outside but from within.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Mark 7:37 in the response to Jesus' miracles?
questions.explanation: The astonishment at Jesus doing all things well in Mark 7:37 highlights His perfect goodness in healing and restoring people.

questions.question: How does Mark 7:27-29 illustrate a redemptive-historical connection regarding Gentile inclusion?
options: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles in God's salvation through faith.
It excludes Gentiles from God's promises.
It limits salvation to Israelites only.
It requires Gentiles to observe Jewish ritual law first.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles in God's salvation through faith.
questions.explanation: Jesus' interaction with the Syrophenician woman in Mark 7:27-29 anticipates the gospel extending to Gentiles who believe.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 7:11-13 teach about human traditions and their effect on God's law?
options: Human traditions can nullify the effect of God's law when obeyed in place of it.
Traditions always complement and support God's law.
Traditions have no influence on obedience to God's law.
God's law is flexible to accommodate traditions.
questions.correctAnswer: Human traditions can nullify the effect of God's law when obeyed in place of it.
questions.explanation: Mark 7:11-13 describes how the 'Corban' tradition allowed people to avoid honoring parents, thus making God's word ineffective by tradition.
